review_title: Il mio primo rigenerato Amazon, vi racconto tutto.Il mio primo rigenerato Amazon, vi racconto tutto.
review_comment: Ero molto titubante nel fare questo acquisto, soprattutto alla luce di alcune recensioni che ho letto proprio qui. Ma, confidente nel fatto che in un modo o nell'altro comunque Amazon ti tulela, alla fine ho vinto la diffidenza e ho comprato un iphone XS 64 Gb color oro dal venditore NEGOZIOREALE. La consegna è stata rapida, circa 3 giorni lavorativi. Come potete vedere dalle foto la scatola non è originale così come non lo sono gli accessori, ma questo è chiaramente specificato nella scheda del prodotto quindi tutto ok. Veniamo all'oggetto della recensione: l'iphone. Una volta tirato fuori dall'orrenda bustina di plastica che lo conteneva, l'ho accuratamente ispezionato rilevando un piccolo segno marcato (circa 1x1 mm) nella parte superiore sinistra dello schermo, dove il display si unisce al notch. A questo si aggiunge un piccolissimo segno (non so come altro definirlo) tra lo schermo e la scocca, nella parte inferiore sinistra. Entrambi i segni sono pressocchè invisibili ad una prima occhiata, occorre esaminare con cura il telefono per rilevarli. Il resto (scocca, schermo, bordi, ecc) è come nuovo. Amazon Renewed dichiara che il telefono "non presenta imperfezioni estetiche visibili tenendo il prodotto a una distanza di 30 centimetri", e direi che la promessa è stata assolutamente mantenuta, ben oltre le aspettative. Esaurita la parte estetica, accendiamo il telefono: l'avvio è immediato, i colori, la luminosità e la presenza dell'opzione True Tone mi fanno pensare che il display è originale Apple, difatti la mancanza del True Tone è solitamente indice di un display non originale o quantomeno più economico di quelli normalmente usati da Apple. Anche il codice IMEI riportato fisicamente sul "cassettino" della Sim corrisponde a quello indicato nelle informazioni del telefono, cosa che mi permette di ipotizzare che il telefono non è il risultato di un assemblaggio di più pezzi provenienti da altri telefoni. La configurazione è avvenuta senza difficoltà e dopo un accurato test di tutta la sensoristica e delle varie parti (Face Id, prossimità, luminosità, touch & 3d touch, giroscopi, tasto muto, volume, power, flash, ricarica wireless, altoparlanti, ecc ecc) non ho rilevato malfunzionamenti o problemi di alcun genere. Il telefono è arrivato con iOs 14.8, versione che se non ricordo male è stata rilasciata intorno a settembre 2021. Analizzando il seriale è possibile determinare l'anno di produzione: il mio nuovo amico risulta essere stato assemblato a Chengdu intorno alla seconda metà di settembre 2018. Facendo due conti, il telefono è rimasto "in giro" da settembre 2018 a settembre 2021, poi non è stato più aggiornato e quindi presumo utilizzato. La batteria presenta una capacità massima dell'80%, in linea a quanto indicato nelle condizioni del prodotto su Amazon. Di sicuro è stato usato non poco, ma il fatto che possa leggere quel valore è un altro ottimo indicatore, significa infatti che la batteria è ancora quella originale, altresì avrei un avviso di "batteria non originale". La scocca posteriore è priva del marchio CE, che di solito identifica i telefoni nati per il mercato Europeo. Ma niente paura, in questo caso significa solo che questo telefono era originariamente destinato al mercato americano o asiatico. Tuttavia, poichè la fotocamera non produce il rumore dello scatto quando è in modalità silenziosa, propendo per il mercato USA. In quello cinese infatti, se non è cambiato qualcosa, i telefoni devono per legge emettere sempre il rumore dello scatto fotografico, così da impedire scatti "rubati". Dura lex, sed lex! Infine faccio una delle ultime ma più importanti prove, vado sul sito Apple e tramite codice seriale verifico la garanzia: e qui ecco la sorpresa (bella)! Non solo il prodotto è regolare, non ci sono allarmi e il seriale è corretto, ma risulto addirittura coperto dall'AppleCare+ fino al 17 di questo mese, mica male :-). Concludo (finalmente, direte voi!): in questo momento sono estremamente contento del mio acquisto, l'iphone è praticamente nuovo e funziona bene. Direi un bel 5 stelle tanto ad Amazon quanto al venditore NEGOZIOREALE, che hanno superato le mie aspettative. Se state leggendo questa recensione, e non importa quando, significa che il telefono sta continuando a funzionare bene. Al primo accenno di problema state sicuri che verrò subito qui ad aggiornare la mia recensione. review_comment: I received the phone within 2 days of ordering. The packaging was fine and initially it appeared to be in great condition. However, I checked the battery health on the first day which stated “Important Battery Message: Your battery’s health is significantly degraded.” The Maximum Capacity for the battery was 78%. No problem, I thought, because one of the reason’s I bought from Amazon is that the phone was advertised “to have a battery which exceeds 80% capacity relative to new” and was “Guaranteed by Amazon” to be “eligible for replacement or refund within 90 days of receipt if you are not satisfied. “ Well clearly, I was not satisfied to receive a phone with a significantly degraded battery. So, I called Amazon Customer service to explain the problem and request a replacement. I did this on the same day I received the phone. The representative was helpful and told me he would send out a replacement immediately, and even upgrade the shipment method for no extra charge. He also told me, both in conversation and in writing to “use the box the replacement comes in to return the original.” That way, I would not be without a phone while waiting for the replacement to arrive. The day the replacement was scheduled to arrive and but had not, I called Amazon customer service back to inquire about the status. Much to my surprise, I was told the replacement phone order had been cancelled by the third-party seller because the original had not been returned. This irritated me for two reasons: (1) I had never been notified the replacement order had been cancelled—apparently, had I not called Amazon was simply going to drop the issue, and (2) I was specifically told by Amazon Customer Service that I did not need to return the original until the replacement was received. I told the agent this was unacceptable and wanted the replacement sent to me, as had been previously arranged. When it became clear that she would not be able to help me, I asked to speak with her manager. After providing her with my phone number, she said her manager would call me back. That phone call never happened. The following day I called Amazon customer service again, now the third time trying to get this issue resolved. I explained the steps I had taken thus far and was put on hold so the representative could verify if my replacement order “was legit.” When I asked what “legit” meant, she said she needed to verify if this was unusual activity on the account because it was a phone purchase. review_comment: I bought the phone on October 26, 2024. It looked to be in like new condition so originally I was happy with the purchase. Within a couple weeks it started giving me black screen where the phone was on and working but the screen was black and I couldn't use it at all. I contacted Amazon and they connected me to The Networkstore who said they were willing to give me a PARTIAL REBATE which would not help at all since I would still need a new phone and it's clear to me that this phone was defective before I ever received it. The next morning the phone was back working normally and so (dummy me) I let it go. Long story short, the phone got worse and worse, taking longer to "fix itself" until right after the return date ended in 3 months the phone screen started flashing and going to black screen even worse and by January, the phone was mostly unusable. 3 months. Now it's just completely dead. The Networkstore told me when I first contacted them (when the black screen first happened) that if it continues happening, they would be willing to help (along with the PARTIAL REFUND). After the return date expired and I again contacted them, they told me that they only meant they would help me get the screen working again. I had already tried everything possible. It's clearly a damaged phone not a software problem. The phone is dead and nothing short of a replacement will fix this. I did nothing to damage the phone. It was put in a full case the minute it was unpacked and was never dropped or mistreated in any way. For the most part it just sat on my desk in my office. It's obvious to me that this phone was ready to go out when they sold it. I know buying a refurbished phone is a risk but I think we should be able to assume that any parts that could go bad have been replaced so although it is a used phone, the parts that can go bad have been replaced. This company obviously does not do that and I will never use them again. Lesson learned. I do not recommend this company at all but if you do buy from them and your phone starts acting strange, contact them immediately and demand to return the phone. If you wait, you will lose your chance and will have wasted your money.

review_comment: The phone I received was by all estimations brand new. Not a mark on it and fully charged. However, being new to the Apple World, I can honestly say Windows & Android are both in plain, simple, super easy to understand English. Apple is not. Even its keyboard is not a full Standard Keyboard, like it is with Windows & any Google machine. Android is Google, that's why I say it that way. No getting around it. Just keeping it short & to the point. Apple's iPhone keyboard takes extreme amount of effort to use because it is not the Standard keyboard of every other operating system. Thankfully, I was able to connect a Bluetooth keyboard to it. Otherwise, it's a serious no-go for keyboard use. As for Apple's iPhone Touchscreen, again, I find it sorely lacking. There's no such thing as the simple pinch & zoom on it. That particular luxury seems to be found only within the Camera & Picture sections. You'd think it'd at least be within the iBook section but it's not. On most everything Windows or Google, every app is not just touch & activate, but also affords the luxury of pinch & zoom as well as easy swipe & easy app close & dismiss. Can't say that about the Apple iPhone. And for some unknown reason its WiFi also keeps turning itself on. I can't seem to keep it off no matter how often I manually turn it off. For Apple being so USER-FRIENDLY, I cannot at all say that it is. In fact, IT IS ANYTHING BUT USER-FRIENDLY. If the Apple World was so user-friendly, then it would be a very simple and easy transition from the Windows or Google platform to Apple. And I can honestly say it is Not at all simple or easy. I was so hoping it would be as simple & easy as my Windows machine & Android phone, but sadly, it's actually quite maddening. If you enjoy Kindle reads, you'll need to install the app for it. But I can also tell you, Apple's iBook seriously pales in comparison to Kindle. Ironically, the Google Search Engine is installed on Apple's iPhone but Kindle is not. I avoid Google anything & everything as much as can be done. But for Apple to deny Amazon's Kindle Apple on its phones, seems almost a crime. I have yet to install the Kindle reading app or to test out the camera on the iPhone. When I do I'll update my review. But currently I can't say it's anything to brag about. And I most certainly did not expect to see Google's Search Engine/Web Browser on it. Size wise, it's the exact same size as my Sony Xperia Z3v. It still functions quite well. Not perfect, but well enough for me since I have it locked to call, text, Kindle reads & camera. I can easily read, pinch & zoom & highlight my Kindle reads, pictures & text messages on it. Can only do that with pictures on the iPhone. So for it being so great, I actually find it quite limiting. Not because it's an iPhone, but because the Apple creators decided to create a platform that is quite complex and extremely arduous to use. Apple created its own "language" that must be learned in order to navigate the complexities of its Eco-system. Even now, trying to login to the Apple App Store, no keyboard appears so I can actually install Apps necessary for my personal use. Yet you're required to sign in to it. How can you sign into the App Store when NO KEYBOARD APPEARS TO LET YOU?! So, even if I did not want to use the phone feature, but instead use it as a computer tablet, I cannot because it won't let me login to the App Store. ... Like I said, to anyone new to the Apple world, it's quite a infuriatingly maddening conundrum. If Apple wants to gain new customers and retain them, then Apple needs to change how it operates. And if Apple is supposed to be the safest of all online platforms, then it should not sport Google's web browser. The phone I received was/is like brand new. Operating it though, takes considerable patients as it is quite the learning curve. It should not be so difficult to transition from Windows, Android or Google to Apple. They all made sense to everybody from the moment they came out because they were in simple English and easily understood and simple to navigate because of it. Apple on the other hand, not by a long shot. Even Apple's touchscreen capabilities sorely lacks in comparison. And that's sad. You'd think their touchscreen capabilities would be at least on-par with Windows, Google & Android but it is not. You'd think Apple's touchscreen capabilities might even be better than Windows, Android & Google, but no. Thus far I can find nothing to brag about regarding Apple anything. I was so hoping to find something better about Apple. Instead, I'm greatly disappointed and left seriously frustrated. The iPhone itself came fully charged and appears in brand new condition. It also came with an original Apple Charger. I give the seller a stellar 5 star rating, along with the iPhone I received. I give Apple itself a mediocre 3, even 2 star rating. So to anyone new to the Apple world, maybe an iPad would be easier to use. I started with a phone since I need both a new phone & a new computer and figured Apple would be a serious upgrade to Windows and for sure compared to Google's Android. ... Apple is not at all user-friendly to a first time user. Only Windows, Google & Android can actually claim user-friendly bragging rights, from day one for any first time user. Apparently I need either direct Apple support or YouTube's Apple education in order to learn how to make the best use of this phone. I don't fault the phone for anything. It's an Apple thing. It's very nearly like you gotta go to MIT to learn it. And that's just not right. Will update as I learn how to navigate Apple's world & extremely clunky Eco-system. 1st Time Apple iPhone User Assessment. - Phone - good. - can't give it high marks due to Apple itself. Apple - not worth all the money & certainly nothing to brag about.

My thoughts: CAMERA The majority of happy, giddy, ecstatic iPhone Air owners are not content creators and think the iPhone Air is awesome. YouTube reviewers depend on their mobile phones to produce video and photos and are not the best judge of the iPhone Air that isn't the very best at producing media. I am not a content creator, but was a professional photographer many years and I am extremely happy with the photos the Air produces. I am retired now and no longer need to shoot in RAW for extensive editing. My previous iPhone 15 Pro took very good photos, but I had to spend time editing in order to back off of the extreme automated processing of the phone's software algorithims. I shot photos at a birthday party at night, outdoors, only lit by string lighting and found the photos to be very natural, not overly processed, well exposed with an absence of grain, even cropping in 3-5x. AUDIO Yes, the Air does not play with stereo speakers. But it is very loud and clear and basically when not using my airpods or using airplay to a bluetooth speaker, it is just fine, no issues. Think about it, how often do you depend on your phone to play loud stereo music? You can always stream to a bluetooth stereo speaker or home stereo or wear your airpods. BATTERY I do a lot of streaming music and podcasts during the day 2-4 hrs worth, receive/answer emails, a lot of texts and take photos and send via iMessage and I'm finding my battery still has 30-50% battery left at 6pm. I don't typically put my phone on a charger during the day and by 6pm I'm ready to eat dinner and relax in the evening so sitting my phone on a magsafe charger stand is an easy way to finish out the day. I did buy Anker's Magsafe power bank that matches the iPhone Air (white) but I've not used it much, more out of convenience because I had it rather than as a necessity. Without a case, it is very slippery and for that reason alone I ended up buying an extremely thin Aramid case from Pitaka to increase the grip. I wasn't worried too much about scratches as I am very careful with my phones, but now I admit, I can relax alittle and I believe the case actually improved the look of the AIR rather than detracted. There wasn't a reason to upload a phone of the phone, you can see those everywhere.

review_comment: I ordered an Amazon Renewed refurbished iPhone Air 256GB (unlocked) from Amazon in March 2026. Apple initially released the iPhone Air in September 2025, so any given unit couldn't be more than 6 months old. For that reason I took a chance by ordering a unit in "Excellent" condition, rather than "Premium" condition, for $80 less. (As of a week later, Excellent units are even cheaper compared to Premium units.) The phone arrived in perfect condition. Not a scratch on it. And even better: its battery health/capacity is 100%, which is far better than Amazon promises for "Excellent" condition units ("Battery: >80% of original battery life"). The OS reports that the phone was first used in October 2025, and only went through 7 battery cycles. So, it seems like it's a unit that someone bought new and returned almost immediately. In my experience, these "Amazon Renewed" phones come from a variety of vendors. My iPhone Air came from "T4C We Track Serial Numbers." --Yes, weird name (maybe a warning to buyers who might try to swap phones by returning a different phone?). But they provided a perfect product. As to the iPhone Air, I settled on it after trying a few different phones, including the iPhone 15 Pro Max, the iPhone 16e, the iPhone 16 Plus, and the iPhone 17e. I had always thought of the iPhone Air as a terrible compromise: larger (but not largest) screen, lesser camera, and far less battery capacity. However, I wanted a slightly larger screen than the standard 6.1 inches, and I don't really prioritize my phone's camera. Plus, I also don't use my phone so much, every day, that I need huge battery capacity. So, after finding that the iPhone 16e's and iPhone 17e's screens were too small, and that the iPhone 15 Pro Max was just way too bulky and heavy, I gave the iPhone Air a chance. I found that the iPhone Air's larger screen (6.5 inches), lighter weight, and dramatically thinner frame make it really pleasant to handle for light, everyday use. And the single-lens camera and lower battery capacity are sufficient for my needs. You can put a nice case on it, and it still feels way thinner than any other iPhone.

review_comment: Buying a used phone can be an anxiety filled experience - you read the reviews and hope that you're one of the happy customers and are lucky enough to get an "as advertised product." You have to take a chance. I did and the phone arrived quickly and with an unexpected charger and cord - generic box and bubble wrap. The phone was listed as in "excellent" and it truly was without a mark, dent or scratch. Several hours of backing up, transferring data and sim - now the phone is truly working and picking up where the prior phone handed off to the latest one. The challenge of course is you have a new phone - and its always a bit steep for the first few days trying to learn the new hardware/software and audit that the used phone does not have some hidden defect that is going to cost you more time and money. So, I'm happy for a few days and then one evening I discover that the bottom speaker (the top earpiece speaker is actually called the receiver) was not working well. scratchy and little to no volume - this had missed my attention entirely. A panic search online revealed Apple 12 speaker problems and them being repaired by Apple - crap! I went to a repair shop the next day, they ran Apple diagnostics on the phone and sure enough - speaker needed to be replaced - $120 for generic parts, $180 for Apple parts - they're not familiar with the Apple repair program (found out later that was for receiver speakers) - so this is half of the cost of the phone. No I'm committed to the new phone, don't want to lose it, but don't want to pay this either. Reach out to seller and explain the issue - they can even confirm the Apple diagnostic through the serial number - They offer $25 refund if I'll keep the phone. - So this tells me that they don't run diagnostics on the phones themselves - or do and hope that people will simply miss small items or accept them once they have sweat equity in the phone - or, it's all honest and by buying/selling a used phone both parties are taking a gamble. I chose to believe the latter. And accepted their offer. And here's the takeaway - the speaker now works - once in a while I might think I hear some scratchy, but unsure due to surrounding conditions. So for now, it's good, we'll see how long it lasts - but if I have to get it repaired - I took a chance - I say take a chance - you might get a perfect phone and save a lot in the meantime - I typically stay a few models behind the curve and benefit from software updates and people abandoning perfectly working phones for the latest models - AT&T typically had new old stock and I took advantage of that, but I have a grandfathered plan that they no longer make good money on, so I'm no longer eligible for that. Hope your experience is a good one - all the best, Don

review_comment: iPhone 16 Pro Amazon Premium Renewed is a Gem The iPhone 16 Pro in Desert Titanium is a slightly heavier phone from any of the previous versions (non max) but the most refined phone yet for us. This marks a handful of times since we’ve gone through Amazon Premium and it delivered for us again with no visible blemishes, with 100% battery life and 1 battery cycle count. (1 cycle =1 battery cycle count of 100% battery drain in a given period). This feature was a new discovery for us, as Apple only began making the cycle count directly visible to users starting with the iPhone 15 lineup. This Renewed Premium unit arrived in pristine condition, offering a high-end feel With 512GB of storage, it provides ample storage making it an exceptional value for those seeking flagship performance without the brand-new price tag. It came with a charging cable (type C-type C), but without the USB-C charging adapter/output. I believe for Amazon Premium Renewed it normally comes with the package but that wasn’t going to be a deal breaker. What Sets the 16 Pro Apart The 16 Pro introduces several meaningful hardware and software evolutions: • Camera Control Button: A new, dedicated tactile sensor on the side that allows for instant camera access and sliding gestures to adjust zoom, exposure, and depth of field. • A18 Pro Chip: Built specifically for Apple Intelligence, this chip handles complex AI tasks locally, which we haven’t taken advantage of. • Larger Display & Thinner Bezels: The screen has expanded to 6.3 inches without significantly increasing the phone's footprint, due to the thinner borders • 48MP Ultra Wide Camera: A massive jump from the previous 12MP sensor, allowing for stunning macro photography and high-detail wide shots. In addition, the zoom feature is amazing, physical 5x zoom and up to 25x digital zoom for photos; videos is up to 15x. Data Transfer Experience Moving 200GB + of data proved to be a bit of a hurdle, specifically when using the standard wireless "Quick Start" method. We encountered repeated connectivity drops and inconsistent progress over WiFi; after a few unsuccessful attempts we decided to opt for a wired connection via PC and ITunes. We used a standard USB-C cable (not the high-speed USB 3.0 or 4.0 variant) • Method: Wired USB-C to USB-C (Standard Speed) • Data Size: ~200GB+ • Total Time: Approximately 3 hours-4 hours There was definitely a significant wait time; although the wired method proved to be reliable, but also requiring a 2 step process, backing data from the old phone to PC then restoring to new phone. A more efficient solution for the wired method is to use the “Super Speed” cables such as USB 3.0 variants or USB 4. Subsequent backups and restorations required a fraction of the time. As of the 3rd week of April 2026, even after a full quarter of heavy use, our iPhone 16 Pro is performing just as smoothly as day 1; the battery health still holds at 100% and the battery cycle is now 120. We are quite pleased with the purchase and how seamlessly the device has been working thus far!

review_title: Für 120 € ein wirklich super Kauf – perfekt für die OmaFür 120 € ein wirklich super Kauf – perfekt für die Oma
review_comment: Ich habe das iPhone SE der 3. Generation mit 64 GB in Mitternacht im Jahr 2026 als generalüberholtes Gerät für meine Oma gekauft und bin wirklich positiv überrascht. Gerade für 120 € bekommt man hier meiner Meinung nach noch erstaunlich viel Smartphone fürs Geld. Das Gerät ist natürlich nicht mehr das neueste iPhone, aber für den vorgesehenen Zweck absolut ausreichend und auch 2026 noch problemlos brauchbar. Für jemanden, der hauptsächlich telefoniert, Nachrichten schreibt, Fotos macht, WhatsApp nutzt und gelegentlich im Internet unterwegs ist, reicht die Leistung vollkommen aus. Durch die kompakte Größe und den Home-Button ist es außerdem gerade für ältere Menschen angenehm und unkompliziert zu bedienen. Der Zustand des generalüberholten Geräts ist ebenfalls sehr gut. Das Gehäuse sieht wirklich sehr ordentlich aus und weist kaum sichtbare Gebrauchsspuren auf. Am Display sind zwar ein paar kleinere Kratzer vorhanden, diese sind aber im Alltag überhaupt nicht störend und fallen bei eingeschaltetem Display praktisch nicht auf. Insgesamt macht das iPhone einen deutlich besseren Eindruck, als ich es bei einem generalüberholten Gerät in dieser Preisklasse erwartet hätte. Auch der Akku hat noch 91 % Restkapazität, was für ein gebrauchtes bzw. generalüberholtes Gerät absolut in Ordnung ist. Für die Nutzung meiner Oma reicht die Akkuleistung problemlos aus und ich sehe bei diesem Wert keinen Grund, den Akku direkt tauschen zu lassen. Die Einrichtung war wie bei einem iPhone gewohnt unkompliziert und auch die Performance ist für den Alltag noch völlig ausreichend. Besonders positiv finde ich, dass man für relativ wenig Geld ein richtiges iPhone mit Touch ID, guter Kamera, kompakter Bauweise und weiterhin brauchbarer Leistung bekommt. Fazit: Wer 2026 ein günstiges, kleines und zuverlässiges Smartphone für einen eher normalen Alltagsgebrauch sucht, macht mit dem iPhone SE 3. Generation meiner Meinung nach noch immer einen guten Kauf. Für 120 € war es für meine Oma jedenfalls eine hervorragende Wahl. Der sehr gute optische Zustand und die 91 % Akkukapazität haben den positiven Eindruck noch einmal bestätigt. Von mir daher ganz klar 5 Sterne.

review_title: Good product, not so good packaging.

While they are both in decent physical and electronic condition and function as intended, I do have some concerns regarding their shipping packaging. Each phone was shipped in its own small box, which included everything necessary: the phone, charger block, charging cable, and documentation. However, the "iPhone SE 3rd Gen" phones are smaller than most common iPhones, and the recessed area in the box is meant to hold the larger iPhone variants. As a result, the phones were able to move around during shipping, potentially leading to damage. Additionally, there were no plastic slipcovers over the phones, leaving the screens completely exposed to scratches from the internal box lid. This comes across as very lazy and cheap. Another issue is that these two individual boxes were placed inside a FedEx box that was far too large. There was no foam or bubble wrap inside this main box to prevent the two smaller boxes from moving around during transit. While I am pleased with the phones and everything worked out in my case, I worry that others may not be as fortunate. Shipping boxes pass through many locations and hands before they arrive at their destination. They have the potential to get dropped and thrown around plenty of times. Improved packaging methods should be considered for these electronics, especially given the amount of money customers spend on them.

Not to mention the charging cable that came with it didn’t work. Anyway, to the pressing issue here I did what I would normally do when setting up a new iPhone and followed the prompts to transfer my data through the cloud onto this device. However, due to the phone’s software being completely outdated (ios18, we’re on 26) it caused the phone to completely glitch out midway and got extremely hot. I couldn’t swipe up to input my passcode to proceed with the installation process. Heck, I couldn’t even force restart it. (quickly press the volume up, volume down immediately after and press and hold the power button until you see the Apple logo) I was almost at my wits end. Fast forward, the device is still glitchy so I reached out to Amazon Customer Care and was advised that I should take it into Apple and if they couldn’t do anything then to proceed with returning it. I obviously didn’t wanna do that. So I attempted to research the issues and after being pulled between Apple’s forum and Reddit’s forum, I decided to put the iPhone in DFU mode. This mode allows you to update and restore the phone via a computer. So boom, it’s in DFU mode and i’m still struggling! So I contact Apple but of course before doing so I see if they’re able to replace a software defective device out of warranty and of course it was a hard no. At this point, I’m ready to give up and just return it but after letting it die out (due to overheating) I let it charge overnight and said “let’s give this oneee more try.” So, I plugged it back into my computer.. same issue. It would pretend to restore and update the device but I would get an error message midway and couldn’t get my phone out of DFU. Only way to get it out was by completing the restoration. Anyway, I looked up the error message it mentioned that it could be a software issue (tell me something i don’t know 🤷🏽‍♀️) or it could be a charger cable issue.. Hmm 🤔 So I switched charging cables (even bought a new one that I would later use) and low and behold the update and restoration finally WORKED… So all in all, I say all of that to say; if you’re having issues with accessing and fully using your new iPhone. It’s more than likely because its software is extremely outdated. What worked for me: Put your phone in DFU mode (look it up if unsure how). Download either Apple Devices (Windows) or iTunes (Mac). While in DFU mode, plug the device up using a USB to lightning Apple Certified cable. A prompt will display saying error something would you like to proceed with restoring or updating? Click “restore” and then “update and restore” (for some reason it didn’t work clicking update first) it’ll take some time but after that it should go through the process of updating and restoring back to the factory settings and then you can proceed with setting the iPhone up as normal. (important!!! the cable needs to be APPLE CERTIFIED not the one from sheetz up the street) I haven’t experienced any delays or issues since updating to the latest version of iOS but i’m giving 3 stars because 1.) the charger it came with didn’t work. and 2.) because i feel like a little help card should’ve been included considering it didn’t have the latest version of iOS on there. review_comment: Today is Wednesday, August 20, 2025. I ordered the iPhone 13 Pro Max, Alpine Green, 256GB – Unlocked, Renewed (Excellent Condition). Unfortunately, my experience was disappointing. When I finally opened the package, the phone was the wrong color (Silver instead of Alpine Green) and had noticeable scratches and chips around the camera lens and aluminum frame. While some wear is expected on a refurbished phone, this was advertised as “Excellent Condition,” and I expected better. To be fair, I still tested the phone. The screen looked great with almost no scratches, the phone screen sensitivity could have been more proactive, and the back glass was in good condition. As a busy college student, I don’t have the time to send the phone back, but I do feel let down. I’ll likely have to spend another ~$100 to replace the battery at my university’s tech repair shop. Overall, I’m leaving 4 stars because the phone does function well and matches the storage capacity I ordered, but the wrong color, poor battery health, and condition not matching the description made this purchase very frustrating. My advice: check the IMEI, serial, SIM restrictions, and battery health right away when buying renewed iPhones, and read the reviews carefully before purchasing. P.S. I purchased a screen protector separately for extra protection. Also, note that the box only included a USB Lightning cable — no charging adapter. If you don’t already have one, I recommend buying an adapter or a complete charger along with the phone.

review_comment: I purchased an Amazon Renewed iPhone 14 Pro Max (128GB, Deep Purple) in Excellent condition because I was willing to pay extra for a device that was supposed to be thoroughly inspected and fully functional. Unfortunately, the phone I received was nowhere near "Excellent." The biggest issue is the camera system. One of the main reasons I chose the iPhone 14 Pro Max was for its three-camera setup. However, only one camera works properly in Photo mode. In Video mode, two cameras work, while the third doesn't work at all. The 0.5x ultra-wide camera is completely unavailable, and the 5x zoom function doesn't work either. This is especially frustrating because I'm an up-and-coming mechanic, and I regularly use the 0.5x camera to take photos in tight spaces while working on customers' vehicles. It's an important tool for my job, not just a feature I wanted. I upgraded from an iPhone 13 Pro Max where two of the cameras had failed, so I was excited to finally have a phone with all three cameras working. Instead, I ended up with another phone that has camera issues. At that point, I could have saved money by buying an iPhone 14 Plus with only two cameras and probably received a phone that actually worked. Another concern was that the phone was not properly factory reset. The packaging states that Amazon Renewed devices are supposed to be factory reset before being resold. However, when I powered it on, it started up like a normal phone instead of taking me through the initial setup process. It appeared the previous owner had simply signed out of their Apple ID rather than the phone being completely erased and reset. I contacted Amazon Customer Support to request a replacement since the phone was defective. I was told there were no more iPhone 14 Pro Max devices in Excellent condition available to send as a replacement. However, when I checked the same Amazon listing, it still showed the exact same phone in Excellent condition available for purchase. I don't understand why replacements weren't available when the listing indicated more were in stock. I would have been happy to return the defective phone in exchange for a properly functioning one. I understand that Amazon Renewed products are used, and I wasn't expecting a brand-new phone. However, I did expect to receive the condition I paid for and a device with all advertised features working correctly. A phone with a partially functioning camera system should never pass inspection as "Excellent," especially when customers are paying a premium for that condition. Overall, this experience was extremely disappointing. Amazon Renewed is supposed to give customers confidence that devices have been inspected and tested. Based on my experience, the inspection process failed, and customer service did not provide a reasonable solution.

review_comment: This was my first purchase of a "premium renewed" smartphone. The Amazon description says "Tested for battery health and guaranteed to come with a battery that exceeds 90% of original capacity." On the iPhone Pro 13 I received, the battery was 90 percent — it didn't "exceed" that number. Ultimately I returned this phone for two reasons: First the pictures look over-sharpened in some instances and almost like a painting in others. Having come from a much older phone that did not over-process the images, I was shocked to see that the HDR was so aggressive. I thought I had nowhere to go but up after such a long time between upgrades, only to learn this has apparently been a trend in iPhone cameras in recent years. The only way I was going to obtain the menu option to turn off HDR was to drop back to an 11 or 12, so I bought the 12 Pro instead, which unlike this phone — which took a week to arrive — shipped in one day. I am happier with the fact that the Pro 12 is lighter weight and slimmer, with a better sense of balance thanks to the fact that the camera bumps are smaller. The iPhone Pro 13 features the older emergency SOS function but it is only as good as one's cell tower connectivity, whereas the 14 and newer also have SOS and roadside assistance functionality via satellite. Based on where I live (mountains, bad cell coverage) I was torn between this purchase and the iPhone 14 Pro series, especially after I realized that a third party seller here on Amazon was offering a "excellent condition" renewed model for what I paid for this older model. Having said this, the iPhone Pro 14 has had reports of overheating and/or lackluster battery performance compared to the iPhone 13 Pro. I also like the fact that the iPhone 13 Pro does NOT have the "always on" screen common to newer Pro models. Another notable difference is that the iPhone 13 Pro (and earlier) have a physical SIM tray whereas the newer 15 Pros are eSIMs. Finally, the iPhone Pro 13 and earlier uses a lightening cord vs. USB-C on current-generation iPhones. (I'm not interested in using a different charging cord/setup than my spouse, especially while traveling.) The Verdict I very much appreciate the excellent cosmetic appearance — there were no scratches or gouges to be found anywhere on the phone I received — but keeping the Pro 13 was not an option. In a video I took of a flock of birds flying just after the sun set behind a hillside, I could make out a round dust spot visible against the cloudless, pale gold sky — dead center in the bottom of the frame (landscape mode). Honestly, I probably never would have seen it in broad daylight because the HDR takes the blue sky and darkens it down so much the dust spot would have been masked — but the light I was shooting against at dusk was just a tad bit paler than the dust spot, allowing me to appreciate that the lenses were not in the perfect shape they initially appeared. Upon further inspection, using a flashlight, I noted some kind of residue *behind* two out of the three lenses. (Supposedly these lenses are sealed but per the reviews here mine is not the first report of dust spots in photos.) Overall, I don't feel like I received the "premium renewed" experience, in part because the shipping was slow (nearly four days before Amazon assigned tracking) and battery health was less than expected (others here reported at or near 100%!). Ultimately, I returned the Pro 13 and bought an iPhone Pro 12 from another seller. Not only did I pay less and end up with a slimmer, lightweight phone that feels better in the hand, but I actually like the camera quality better because it is among a very small number of iPhones where it is actually possible to turn off the HDR.

review_comment: First off, I never write reviews, but after my recent experiences I thought this might help some others. Needed to replace an aging IPhone which was still working great, but a lot of apps needing newer IOS. So, not looking for the lastest/greatest, just a good update. Decided IPh 14+ was a good option. Here were my first 3 strikes : 1) I purchased an “Excellent” OPEN BOX phone from Best Buy. It came in a box sealed with Geek Squad tape. When opened, the phone had tons of fingerprints all over it, front and back; not a great first impression. After going through the startup process I was greeted with a screen that informed me that the phone had remote management software installed on it. Basically unusable. 2) I returned it and they replaced it with another “Excellent” OPEN BOX. Same thing – both phones had been previously owned by some company (now out of business) who had loaded remote management software on the phones. So… these are expensive, unusable bricks, and shame on BB/Geek Squad for selling these phones to the public. 3) After that experience I decided to give Amazon a try and bought a phone supplied by WOOT, as I have had good experiences with other Woot purchases. The phone arrived in a beat up generic box with the inside packaging worse than the outside. On the positive side, the phone was cosmetically very good with no obvious scratches, etc. So, everything looked good until I checked the battery health. 81%. NOT GOOD. Yes, it meets the described spec of >80% for their “Excellent” condition, but will going to be into the Apple service condition in a couple of weeks. Returned to Amazon/Woot and waiting for refund. After reading a ton of reviews I decided to give it one more shot and get a “Premium” condition directly from Amazon.com. Most of the reviews of these phones were much better than all of the other vendors. They are definitely more expensive but come with a 365 day warranty vs 90 day and spec at >90% battery life. Phone arrived today. It was VERY nicely packaged in a SEALED shrink wrapped professional looking box. Opened the box and found a phone with what appeared to be the original Apple protective film still in place on the front and back. Battery was dead so after a quick charge I was able to check battery health…… 100% and 0 charge cycles. Basically this is a brand NEW, NEVER USED phone. I can’t say how impressed I was after three bad experiences. I saved a couple $hundred compared to BB or Apple and got a brand new phone ….. It’s all about the journey  !!!

Also during this time, WirelessSource sent me a message claiming my device was iCloud locked: i.e. I didn't wipe the iPhone before returning it. I did wipe the iPhone, and after a few back-and-forth messages and photos, (including one where they claimed the IMEI didn't match the order even though we previously confirmed it did,) I recorded a video of me going to my Apple account and FindMyiPhone and demonstrating that I had wiped the phone and it was no longer on my account. After that video, they confirmed the account removal. While this was happening, I filed an A-z Refund claim with Amazon. I didn't have a whole lot of faith that I would be refunded at this point. While the claim was active, Todd Lewis of The Reputation MD sent me a 'refund contract.' This contract was meant to ensure I returned the iPhone (even though at that point they had already received it back,) and it was also meant to prevent me from defaming the company, although I suspected they would try and leverage the contract to prevent me from leaving a negative review. I am not making a concrete claim, though, it was just a suspicion I had. Like before, no other refund I've done has made me do this, and I ignored the contract despite their daily emails. Eventually, Amazon themselves refunded me, and I chose to let the Better Business Bureau complaint go. I continued to ignore their emails, since attempting to get a refund from them on top of Amazon's would be fraud, and eventually they stopped. I wanted to leave this review to recount my experience with WirelessSource/Magnakom as well as Todd Lewis and The Reputation MD. I've tried to be objective so you can draw your own conclusions. I have provided a compilation of the messages between us, although it may take some zooming to see them all. I hope you find this review helpful, and I hope WirelessSource learns to do better.

review_title: BE AWARE OF THE RISKS - I spent hours fixing Amazons issueBE AWARE OF THE RISKS - I spent hours fixing Amazons issue
review_comment: Updated: since writing the below review, I have received my second 15 pro max renewed premium, set it up, and handled the refund from the first one. Amazon customer support also offered me a generous discount on the new phone for all the hassle (which I somewhat needed to initiate asking for, I doubt they would have offered that to begin with). If I had to do it all over again - I would have still gone this route since apple refurbished hasn’t released this model yet, but moving forward- I will probably order straight from apple refurbished next time or just get a new iPhone. When factoring the discount I got on this one that’s one year old, I paid about 2/3 the cost for this compared to the latest model, so I can’t complain. All that said, in general I am one who much more values my time and ease over saving a quick bucks. Especially if that quick buck saved costs me HOURS of my life in hassle. If you’re like me in that sense - proceed with caution. I trust Amazon will help make it right if you don’t get a great phone as expected, but even if that’s the case, you’re probably in for quite the hoops to jump through in order to make that happen. Here’s my original, unedited review: I ordered the iPhone 15 Pro Max refurbished and it arrived last night. After spending a good 3+ hours setting it up, I realized the lens for the main camera was broken. From the outside, you can’t see any issue. It wasn’t until I opened up the camera app that I actually saw it didn’t work. “Renewed Premium” carries a certain standard with it, and this certainly does not meet that in the slightest. On top of that, upon calling customer support, I was told that I would not be able to do anything unless I deactivated the phone and remove my Apple ID from it. Wouldn’t have been the end of the world if I needed to go back to my other phone for a bit, however, in order to set up this phone with the eSIM, deactivated my previous SIM card. Upon explaining all of that to customer support, I was told there was nothing they could do unless I deactivated this phone (leaving me without a phone until they received this and shipped me a new one) I was then told to call Apple to see what they can do, when honestly, this is their mistake. Either way, I called apple and it was going to be another set of hoops to jump through with scheduling appointments and all that. Plus since I didn’t have apple care, if they needed to repair the camera, I would still be without a phone. So even if Apple was able to help fix this, the issue of me not having a phone would still be there. Had I broken this camera myself - I would certainly except those terms given there’s not much else I could do. However, this was given to me in this condition and for Amazon to leave me with the responsibility of fixing their mistake due to carelessness in inspection and quality control is absurd. So whether I like it or not, I am now STUCK with the responsibility of cleaning this up since my account is connected to this phone now. What at one point could have been a great gift to myself has turned into the biggest hassle I’ve experienced buying/returning anything, probably ever. I’m going to give this one more shot as I’ve now ordered another iPhone from them to be delivered shortly, however, it’s also required me to spend another ~$1000 in having that iPhone sent prior to me getting my refund. This is absolutely ridiculous and unacceptable. Even if this next phone is perfect, I’m likely never going to order from the Amazon refurbished store again. I’ll either go straight to Apple refurbished, or brand new, for any of my future phone/laptop/device purchases. On top of all this hassle, I’ll certainly have to spend another few hours setting up my replacement phone once it arrives. All the time I’ve invested into this so far has NOT been even close worth the “nice discount” on a premium refurbished phone that should have arrived without issue to begin with. Amazon - take note. Change your policies. Making this the customer’s mess to clean up is not acceptable. Potential buyers - BEWARE of the risks. I’ll plan to update this review if anything changes. But like I said, even if the next phone I ordered is perfect, I still give this a 1-star review for all the hassle and lack of responsibility the company took to resolve this. P.s. i’ll also add that I am a quite understanding and peaceful person. The person I spoke with from customer support was doing his absolute best to help me, but this was clearly a bigger issue than he had the power to solve. I requested to have this escalated to upper management and was told the same thing. Whoever is the one making decisions about what can and can’t be done needs to hear about this.

review_title: If at first you get a defective phone, try again if you have the patience.
review_comment: My phone rated Excellent Premium was defective in a way any technician would have identified had it really been tested and reviewed before publishing the phone on Amazon's website. Amazon give the impression that the customer should feel some comfort because of it's rating and because they are Amazon. That doesn't work that way. When you contact Amazon they ask about the problem and then pass on to the seller a very abridged summary. They assure you they will help. But all the conversation between you and Amazon disappears. If you want to preserve this conversation and refer back, or follow up, it is nowhere to be found. They claim to have a buyer/seller message board, but Amazon is invisible and you can't ask for more help. It turns out that part of my biggest problem was how to discover why the phone did not work. I didn't know that an Excellent premium phone can be tested and verified without the updated IOS version being downloaded and installed, and it can't. But no where are you told that. I spent hours on the phone with the carrier and texting with AI because I couldn't even get Apple to acknowledge my Apple account. Then after all my efforts I was locked out for 2 hours! It seems to me this is vital info for a new buyer like me, and it should be included by Amazon in their description. As it turned out the "board" connecting the eSim that issues the signal for cellular to work was defective. But no experts that I consulted realized that a simple test of the eSim is to try to read a Qr code, without a functioning eSim that will not be possible and certainly that is a simple test for verifying a several hundred dollar phone before giving it an Excellent premium rating in Amazon. For several other reasons too lengthy for this review, I now believe Amazon's rating of refurbished phones is BS. And their help is minuscule. Despite that, I ordered a replacement iPhone 15 pro through Amazon, again got suckered in on a non updated IOS, but so far, now that my Apple a/c is recognized, the phone appears to be truly excellent. I knew enough to avoid the extra cost of PREMIUM. Update, I'm still waiting for my refund on the first phone 19 days after paying for it. I've updated my review from one to 3 stars because the replacement phone is in excellent condition as rated, and much more deserving of a Premium designation, which the seller did not claim. I remain disappointed in the Amazon role in the transaction but they do have a large inventory to choose from. Why can't Amazon include in it's sale promotion description a warning to be sure to check whether the phone has the latest IOS upgrade, don't trust the seller. Not knowing to do this cost meat at least half a day all told.

review_title: Probably one of the most practical options out there
review_comment: In brief; The iPhone 13 Mini is the smallest flagship on the market; this makes it the most practical phone for those who mostly use their smartphone as a communication device and little besides. A screen protector is a must. The Renewed Premium phone arrived in excellent condition and has given me no issues in six months of use. I recommend it. In detail: ---Preamble--- I didn't buy a cell phone until mid-2008, and didn't buy a smartphone until early-2019. Both decisions were provoked by starting a new job. I've never been a heavy phone user; I receive less than twenty-five texts from actual humans a year, and maybe a phone call every other month. I only use my smartphone for calls, texts, checking email/calendar, navigation, alarm, and on occasion, checking into events or to take pictures. My app usage is limited to train tickets. As a result, I don't need much from my phone. I like having something fairly powerful, so it will run smoothly for as long as possible before I have to replace it. I didn't want anything too expensive, which is why I ignored Sony's offerings. I wanted a decent support cycle, which is why I ignored the Zenfones. I wanted something with reliable HW, which is why I didn't go with a Pixel. I wanted it to have WiFi calling/texting. I specifically wanted something small and compact, as my main complaint about my prior smartphone was how large it was. I would have replaced it earlier, but it was an Android and since the demise of the Sony Xperia Compact line there were no US-market small Android smartphones produced by anyone. I didn't want to make the transition to the Apple ecosystem, since this would be my one and only Apple device, so I dragged my feet even for a year after my old phone stopped voluntarily connecting to the cell network. Eventually I decided that I spend more time carrying my phone around than using it, and therefore form factor was more important than OS. ---Review--- I would never have purchased this at its original retail price, but it was definitely worth it at $450, particularly with the Amazon Renewed Premium Program. It arrived in a condition indistinguishable from new, at least to my eye. Setup was easy enough, though despite assertions otherwise the automated process of moving Android data to the Apple was not perfectly smooth and I had to make a number of adjustments after the fact. As a result of making this transition, I still run my Google apps on the iPhone - Authenticator, Calendar, Mail, and Maps in particular. I don't plan on changing those any time soon, but it does introduce some confusion into the workflow on the phone. For current Android users, there are some significant downsides. The loss of the ability to customize the environment is painful, even after six months. I am fairly technically capable and so appreciate the ability to make minor tweaks and adjustments to everything, and iOS constantly fights you on this. I would like my small icons back, and my ability to arrange them as I see fit. The lack of robust gesture/tap support, and limited gadget/widget customizability means you need to spend more time navigating than before. iOS's reputation for a janky file system presentation is well deserved, it can be hard to tell where files are going or have gone. In a non-Apple environment, HEIC complicates file storage and backup, though there are workarounds. The messaging app, for who knows what reason, doesn't have an archive option and just lists every conversation you've ever had in one long list on the main page, and requires an extra tap after the swipe to delete anything. There's no easy way to skip or snooze all alarms. All things I can put up with, though for the first month I was rather stroppy. I adapted to the UI quickly, but again I only use very few functions on the phone in my day-to-day life. I was able - with some frustration - to pair a set of Samsung Galaxy Buds, though you can only configure them through an Android device. Build quality seems excellent; however, do not take this phone out of its package unless you have a screen protector waiting for it. I was uncommonly gentle with this thing for the four days I was waiting for the protector to arrive, storing it in a pocket which had a clean cotton handkerchief padding the screen, and I -still- ended up with a significant enough scratch that it is still visible under the screen protector in direct sunlight. Don't risk it. HW and SW performance in contrast is flawless. I agree with the common sentiment that the iOS experience is very smooth, though I may be biased on account of my previous phone being on its way out at the time of transition. Battery life for me is probably two days and well into the third. That sounds good, perhaps, but my screen-on time is very low - I'm guessing between zero and ten minutes a day, with most of it on the low end, the only exception being during navigation. It is not unusual for multiple days to pass where my only interaction with my phone is to turn off the alarm. I would expect longer battery life under such circumstances, but I suppose that so long as it lasts all day it doesn't really matter. Lastly, I would say the sacrifice for the form factor was definitely worth it. I keep my phone in a cargo pocket and it is much lighter and less bulky now, especially when crouching down. 100% worth prioritizing that feature. ---Conclusion--- Like I said above, if you are like me - you are someone who doesn't need a lot of screen real-estate, power, or extensive battery life, but still wants to have the full functionality of a smartphone for irregular use, this is probably the best choice on the market. It was worth the transition from Android and the ongoing annoyance of Apple's eccentricities of design. I would recommend it, and will consider getting the next iPhone Mini, if Apple ever releases one.

We got the phone and it looked great, seemed to work fine. Except it would not connect to cellular. After a week and a half of going round and round with our phone carrier, we finally figured out the phone was not fully unlocked as the listing had set. We initiated a return and were told we would be refunded when the phone was received and checked. I was initially told by the Amazon CSR I spoke to that as a courtesy, they would issue the refund as soon as the item showed it was picked up by UPS. After waiting a few days and no sign of refund, I called again. I was told by this CSR that I was given incorrect info, Amazons policy was to issue the refund when it’s received and checked. OK. So I wait again. I was told that once the phone was received, it could be up to 30 business days for it to be checked and refunded—but it rarely takes that long. I was given the date it was received. More waiting, then a full 30 business days after it had been received I called again to check on refund. It had not been initiated, but that CSR was initiating it. It literally took a full month and a half from the time Amazon received it (not from the time UPS picked it up—from the time Amazon actually received it back at their facility) for my refund to post. And the reason it was being returned was because it was misrepresented in the listing (not being fully unlocked), not because we changed our mind or anything frivolous. That did not matter and there was no courtesy or concession for what was their mistake in the first place. If you do get anything Amazon renewed, beware. If it works (like the 2nd phone we ordered did), it’s great and a wonderful option if you can’t afford fully new. But if there’s a problem you will get the run around, delays and misinformation from Amazon’s CSRs. They claim to stand behind all renewed products, but they will absolutely drag their feet and claim “it’s our policy” while you’re left waiting endlessly. So when it comes to Amazon renewed, don’t be blinded by the great prices and guarantees…it’s definitely “buyer beware”!

review_title: Great iPhones, But Set-up Took A Long Time!
review_comment: This was was an upgrade purchase for my daughter. We don't believe in buying $1,000+ phones for teenagers. Amazon's Refurbished was a welcomed gift! The phone comes well packaged and is in great shape. It works like new, as promised! But, it took us MANY HOURS to finally get this phone set-up and info transfered over. Here are some learned tips for set-up: First, fully charge the new phone and your old phone. If possible, leave them both plugged in during the process. We learned that your old phone needs to be at least 50% charged before it will even start the transfer process. Don't bother backing up your old phone to the iCloud beforehand. It's much faster to wait and do that with the new phone after all is said and done. Your first step, go into the new phone and in Settings, go into General, then update the software to the latest version. We had many issues with the process stalling and then we would finally get an error message? This wasted a lot of time! It's so much quicker to update that software first, though it will take awhile (not lying). Once the software on the new phone is updated, then start the transfer process with your old phone. It will take a while (maybe 30 minutes). Once the whole thing transfers, your new phone will work and everything on the screen will look like your old phone. Here's the one thing we did not think about, you will still need a new SIM card from your Carrier. They are free. Simply go to your Carrier's store and explain that you bought a used phone and they will give you one. After everything is all set-up, call your carrier with your old phone and they will talk you through the process of installing the new SIM into the new phone. They will even test it out with you online until it works. Amazon Refurbished is guarranteed and definitally cheaper than other sites. The phone arrives fast too! After all is said and done, wipe the old phone to factory settings and remove the SIM card. Then you are all set! Newer phone at a cheaper price, it's guarranteed, and my daughter is totally happy with it!

review_title: Amazon exceeded my expectation with this iPhone 14 Pro
review_comment: I did a lot of research before I arrived at this decision to purchase my next iPhone. I’m not the average person that keeps upgrading year after year. I waited a good amount of time before I decided on this decision. And I love Amazon, and when they said that they have a “Renewed Premium” iPhone for sale…they mean it. Apple does not sell Pro variant predecessor models (14 Pro/Pro Max, 13 Pro/Pro Max, etc) but only the newest which are the 15 Plus, Pro/Pro max ) so i had to look online and I found Amazon to have the best deal. I unboxed my iPhone 14 Pro and I couldn’t believe my eyes as to how flawless the phone was. It had zero and i mean ZERO scratches!!! The screen looked good, camera, battery, sound, and the back finish had zero smudges or scratches. For the price, I am absolutely satisfied. I usually bide my time and wait years to pay for a brand new phone but Apple is asking for essentially a price of a mortgage payment for a new phone…it’s unrealistic. Buying refurbished not only saved me money but it’s better for the environment and Amazon does guarantee a 1 year return which is very gracious and I appreciate that, especially when you’re spending almost $1000 on a phone. The packaging was great and came with a USB cable and wall plug. I’m writing this review because i implore others to try out this opportunity because it’s good for your wallet and the environment. This changed the landscape of my cell phone shopping experience because i no longer have to pay full price for an iPhone from Apple. Apple does have a refurbished/clearance section on their website BUT the availability of their models/sizes/colors is scarce and the prices are still hiked up. I do believe Amazon “Renewed Premium” is the key to ensuring that you will get a high quality phone in good condition. The one thing that i found to be dubious of the shopping experience was that within the packaging, there was a card inside of a paper sleeve that had a bunch of checkboxes for the “technician” to check off all of the functions of the phone that were tested/passed and some of the checkboxes were titled “Touchbar” and “Trackpad”…and they were indeed checked on the checklist. But why? This is not a laptop or macbook and there is no “trackpad” or “touchbar” which leads me to challenge the integrity for the “testing” or “refurbishment” procedures at Amazon. Are they just checking all of the boxes to make it look presentably reliable or are they actually testing the functions of the phone? That’s something to consider. I did, however, test it myself and came to conclude that the phone was all good. Would I trust this process and buy another phone from Amazon, absolutely ! I just wanted to point that out.

review_comment: My daughter’s phone died, and it was critical that we replace it because she’s at an age where she ventures out on her own more and more. Having location and the ability for her to call if she needs help was a must. Someone recommended an Amazon renewed iPhone, which was fantastic as our budget didn’t allow for a new phone. We got the phone and it looked great, seemed to work fine. Except it would not connect to cellular. After a week and a half of going round and round with our phone carrier, we finally figured out the phone was not fully unlocked as the listing had set. We initiated a return and were told we would be refunded when the phone was received and checked. I was initially told by the Amazon CSR I spoke to that as a courtesy, they would issue the refund as soon as the item showed it was picked up by UPS. After waiting a few days and no sign of refund, I called again. I was told by this CSR that I was given incorrect info, Amazons policy was to issue the refund when it’s received and checked. OK. So I wait again. I was told that once the phone was received, it could be up to 30 business days for it to be checked and refunded—but it rarely takes that long. I was given the date it was received. More waiting, then a full 30 business days after it had been received I called again to check on refund. It had not been initiated, but that CSR was initiating it. It literally took a full month and a half from the time Amazon received it (not from the time UPS picked it up—from the time Amazon actually received it back at their facility) for my refund to post. And the reason it was being returned was because it was misrepresented in the listing (not being fully unlocked), not because we changed our mind or anything frivolous. That did not matter and there was no courtesy or concession for what was their mistake in the first place. If you do get anything Amazon renewed, beware. If it works (like the 2nd phone we ordered did), it’s great and a wonderful option if you can’t afford fully new. But if there’s a problem you will get the run around, delays and misinformation from Amazon’s CSRs. They claim to stand behind all renewed products, but they will absolutely drag their feet and claim “it’s our policy” while you’re left waiting endlessly. So when it comes to Amazon renewed, don’t be blinded by the great prices and guarantees…it’s definitely “buyer beware”!

review_title: Great iPhones, But Set-up Took A Long Time!
review_comment: This was was an upgrade purchase for my daughter. We don't believe in buying $1,000+ phones for teenagers. Amazon's Refurbished was a welcomed gift! The phone comes well packaged and is in great shape. It works like new, as promised! But, it took us MANY HOURS to finally get this phone set-up and info transfered over. Here are some learned tips for set-up: First, fully charge the new phone and your old phone. If possible, leave them both plugged in during the process. We learned that your old phone needs to be at least 50% charged before it will even start the transfer process. Don't bother backing up your old phone to the iCloud beforehand. It's much faster to wait and do that with the new phone after all is said and done. Your first step, go into the new phone and in Settings, go into General, then update the software to the latest version. We had many issues with the process stalling and then we would finally get an error message? This wasted a lot of time! It's so much quicker to update that software first, though it will take awhile (not lying). Once the software on the new phone is updated, then start the transfer process with your old phone. It will take a while (maybe 30 minutes). Once the whole thing transfers, your new phone will work and everything on the screen will look like your old phone. Here's the one thing we did not think about, you will still need a new SIM card from your Carrier. They are free. Simply go to your Carrier's store and explain that you bought a used phone and they will give you one. After everything is all set-up, call your carrier with your old phone and they will talk you through the process of installing the new SIM into the new phone. They will even test it out with you online until it works. Amazon Refurbished is guarranteed and definitally cheaper than other sites. The phone arrives fast too! After all is said and done, wipe the old phone to factory settings and remove the SIM card. Then you are all set! Newer phone at a cheaper price, it's guarranteed, and my daughter is totally happy with it!

An unadorned white cardboard box labeled "Amazon Renewed" on the top and some device info on the back. Inside, side-by-side, two recessed trays, one for the iPhone (covered by a clear plastic film) and the second for a USB 5V power adapter and 3' Lightning cable. A "OPEN ME FIRST" sleeve with several cards inside: HI THERE, WE'VE GOT YOU COVERED, QUICK START GUIDE, SIM REMOVAL TOOL, and INSPECTION TEST CERTIFICATE. Cosmetically the phone looked brand new. No noticeable blemishes (just a tiny scratch near the Lightning connection). So, after powering on and setting up the iPhone 12, I checked a few things. WiFi and Bluetooth were okay. Face ID okay. The battery was at 81% charge, with a Max Capacity (Battery Health) of 89%. iOS was at version 16.3.1, which I upgraded to 16.4.1, then 16.4.1(a). The back of the box noted "BH 91%" and the Inspection Certificate noted that "Your Device" – A2172 BH91 – was "Tested in New Jersey" on 03/24/2023" and "Battery Health 90%+ confirmed." So, in the time (~6 weeks) between inspection and arrival, this iPhone lost 2% of max battery capacity. Is this typical (as in other reviews)? Is this a big deal? Well, in my case 89% BH probably is good enough. The renewed iPhone 12 is not my primary smartphone. And the fully charged battery lasts longer than my old iPhone SE's. And the 12 has the latest iOS and other more recent hardware and software features (like MagSafe, Precision Finding). The Amazon Renewed Guarantee includes replacement or refund within 1 year of replacement. That's a plus.

review_title: Solid Phone, Frustrating Trade-Offs at This Price
review_comment: I wanted to love this thing. A renewed iPhone 16e at a discount felt like a smart move, modern iOS, A18 chip, USB-C, IP68, the whole package. I talked myself into it. Then I actually used it. The performance is genuinely good. The A18 is fast, apps snap open, and Apple Intelligence works as advertised. Battery life impressed me more than I expected, easily a full day and then some with room to spare. The 6.1-inch OLED display looks great indoors. The camera is where things got real. One lens. Just one. No ultrawide, no macro, no nothing extra. At this price point, even budget Android phones ship with three cameras. Apple made a deliberate choice here and buyers should understand what they are signing up for before clicking add to cart. The design quirks pile up fast. No MagSafe (just standard slow wireless charging), no Dynamic Island, a 60Hz display, and a notch that looks lifted straight from an iPhone 14. The phone also arrived eSIM only, which tripped me up during setup if your carrier or workflow is not ready for that. Cosmetically, the renewed unit was clean and showed no real wear, so no complaints there. The Amazon Renewed program handled the process fine. Ultimately I returned it. Not because it is a bad phone, but because the gap between what this costs and what you actually get compared to a used iPhone 16 is just not wide enough to justify the trade-offs. Do yourself a favor and spend a little more for the real thing, or go further down market intentionally.

review_title: Scary transaction w/ empty delivered box, but Customer Service replaced itScary transaction w/ empty delivered box, but Customer Service replaced it
review_comment: I had not purchased an Amazon Refurbished product before. But we were looking for a large capacity 1TB iPhone 17 Pro, and didn't find one available for under $1300 + tax at local Apple Stores. With the new iPhones coming out at the end of the summer, we didn't want to pay full price, but our old iPhone was full and wasn't working very well. So, during Prime Day sales, we decided to order a Renewed Premium iPhone 17 Pro 1TB from Amazon. It wasn't available for next day or 2 day delivery, but the priced was great under $1300. When delivery came, I was waiting by the front door like a little kid during Christmas. I opened the Amazon box showing 2 items inside and I grabbed the Renewed Premium box and there was no shrink wrap, no sealed close tape to prevent the box from being opened. In my hast, I didn't even record the box opening process. I just flipped open the lid and was shocked to find an empty box with just a charge cable and no iPhone 17 Pro. I looked at the Amazon outside brown box to check for tampering, looked good, one layer of table, not cut open and resealed. I called Amazon Customer service immediately, she said the driver made a mistake and would deliver it the following day (a weekend delivery). My order showed as delivered. - about $1300 and all I had was an emplty box with a USB-C charge cable. That's it. Did I just make the biggest mistake on this on-line order? Why didn't I. record opening the box? I felt bad, and thought driver error??? No way, the outside brown box was sealed. The refurbished box had to have been tampered with in the packing and shipping stage, not during the delivery. I called Amazon Customer Service again, explaining the empty box. They asked for photos which I took shortly after the delivery. They agreed to send a replacement. We got the replacement and were quite happy with it's like new quality. No signs of use, no nics or scratches and it's battery was at 100% capacity with I think 1 cycle on it. Amazon came through with a great replacement. It took several hours to restore and then add it to our account. But all works great now. So, it was a little scary with no product in an empty box, but Amazon Customer Service (my second - third calls) did fix the order and it was a great deal. Look at the refurbished details carefully, and video opening the box and the package contents so you have some evidence on what was was actually in the box. Especially if it is not shrink wrapped or sealed with tape. My video of the replacement didn't show the shrink wrapping well in the photo grab of the opening of the shrink wrap. Thanks to my 2nd and 3rd contact of Customer Service to resolve this purchase. And PS the iPHone 17 Pro is awesome and has lot so space to record kids and concerts.
